Hi Dana,

Thanks for the sync this morning. Per our MAP we agreed to a short, focused validation covering latency, throughput, and TTFT across your expected prompt size distribution and a long-context sweep to quantify max-sequence behavior. I attached the MAP_PerfPlan_ACME_v1.xlsx with the runbook. High-level: 

- Goals: measure p50/p95/p99 token latency, tokens/sec (throughput) at target concurrencies (1, 4, 16), and TTFT for first-token scenarios.
- Long-context sweep: sequences at 2k, 8k, 16k, and 32k tokens; KV-cache warm/cold comparisons.
- Test harness: Redwood dedicated inference cluster (g4dn-like baseline) and a compatible quantized variant we discussed.
- Acceptance criteria: p95 <= 350ms for 2k sequences at conc=4; graceful degradation for 16k/32k with documented fallbacks.

Please confirm the example prompt bucket distributions in tab 'prompt_profile' and attach any canonical prompts you want included. We’ll run a first pass (round1) and share a CSV summary.

Deliverables and dates:
- Round 1 runs and CSV results: by EOD 2026-11-17
- MAP results summary and recommendations: 2026-11-20
- Target close / PO issuance: week of 2026-11-22 (per procurement)

Attachments: MAP_PerfPlan_ACME_v1.xlsx (plan + runbook)

Subject: Re: MAP: ACME performance validation — long-context & KV-cache impact (plan)

Dana — quick follow-up on KV cache and harness details so expectations are aligned for round1: 

- KV warm runs: we simulate a realistic chat session by seeding the KV cache with four prior turns (approx 1.2k tokens total) and then running the test prompt to observe TTFT and subsequent token latency. Cold runs start from an empty KV.
- Measurement approach: TTFT measured from request arrival at the load-balancer to first output byte; token latency measured per generation step and aggregated as p50/p95/p99. Concurrency patterns: single-connection spike tests (1 -> 16) and stable conc buckets (1,4,16).
- Hardware: dedicated cluster (A100-equivalent perf), quantized variant on Ampere T4-like nodes for cost comparison. We’ll note kernel/compilation config used for each run in the CSV.

We started round1 this morning against your provided short/mid prompt buckets. Attached: round1_results_ACME.csv (partial) and kv_cache_latency_chart.png (visual). Early observations:

- Short prompts (<512): p95 token latency ~45ms, tokens/sec ~860
- Mid prompts (512-2k): p95 token latency ~120ms, tokens/sec ~340
- Long prompts (2k): p95 token latency ~310ms at conc=4 (meets target)
- Ultra-long (8k+): tail latency increases non-linearly; KV warm reduces p95 by ~18% vs cold for 8k tests; beyond 16k we observe memory-backed slowdowns and recommend either progressive truncation or staged fallbacks to a streaming model variant.

Questions for you: can we run a single 32k end-to-end test with a realistic turn history? If not, we’ll emulate with contiguous long sequence to map tail behavior.

-Karthik
Principal Engineer, Inference
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MAP: ACME performance validation — long-context & KV-cache impact (initial results)

Dana — attaching a short executive summary (pasted below) and the full CSV in case procurement needs it for cost modeling. We’ll expand on recommendations in the MAP summary on Friday.

Executive summary (round1, dedicated cluster):
- 2k sequence (conc=4): p50=210ms, p95=325ms, p99=620ms; tokens/sec ~290
- 8k sequence (KV-warm): p95 improved from 980ms -> 800ms; throughput decreased ~22% vs 2k workloads
- 16k+ sequences: sustained generation with progressive memory pressure; recommend: a) enable KV cache compaction for chat (saves ~12-15% memory), b) introduce staged fallbacks (streaming-only variant after 12k).

Risk/notes: quantized variant shows ~1.8x lower cost per token with ~10-18% latency degradation at tails — acceptable for background batch workloads but not for interactive-first experiences.

Next steps: we’ll run the 32k emulation if you approve and include the dedicated per-token cost ballpark for purchase order.

-Marissa
Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
